title: Tenant Failover Simulation and Communications Protocol
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the standardized simulation protocol and external/internal communications templates for tenant-level failover drills used during enterprise onboarding, regulatory cutovers, and quarterly resilience validation. It combines operational playbook steps, measurable success criteria, and pre-approved customer and stakeholder communications to ensure consistent execution and evidence capture for compliance audits.

Scope: Applies to Dedicated and Private tenants and to Hosted tenants with enterprise contracts that require documented failover testing. Excludes backend cloud provider maintenance (handled by cloud runbooks) and data-migration-only exercises.

Objectives
- Validate automated failover mechanics across ingress, model-routing, and telemetry fallbacks.
- Exercise on-call and customer-success communications and escalation paths.
- Produce auditable evidence (logs, traces, screenshots, post-run report) for regulatory signoff.
- Surface latent operational gaps in capacity, routing, or observability.

Stakeholders and Roles
- Owner: Customer Success (Aisha Patel) — organizes schedule, customer comms, runbook coordination.
- Oncall Lead: Eng-SRE (Marco Liu) — executes failover actions and runbook steps.
- Runtime SME: Eng-Serving-Runtime (Jordan Reyes) — triages model routing and KV cache issues.
- Telemetry/Observability: Eng-Platform (Dr. Elena Groves) — validates metrics and evidence capture.
- Legal/Compliance: Legal (reviewer) — approves customer-facing wording for regulatory cutovers.

Prerequisites (matrix)
| Item | Owner | Required State | Verification |
|------|-------|----------------|--------------|
| Tenant acceptance tests completed | Customer Success | green | CI test report link |
| Canary telemetry pipeline configured | Eng-Platform | green | sample synthetic trace exists |
| Dedicated failover playbook uploaded to runbook library | Eng-SRE | uploaded | runbook ID: RNBK-FF-01 |
| Customer notification window agreed | CS & Customer | confirmed | signed email chain |

Simulation Types (choose one)
1) Controlled switchover (preferred for cutovers): simulate graceful ingress route shift with customer in read-only window.
2) Chaos-style preemption: simulate GPU preemption to test auto-recovery and fallback to lower-cost model variant.
3) Observability-only drill: no traffic impact; validate alerting and evidence capture.

Success Criteria (all must be met to mark simulation as PASS)
- Traffic reroute success: 100% of new requests routed to fallback lane within the planned 30s window.
- SLOs during failover: p50 latency increase < 2x baseline; p95 < 3x baseline and < 800ms absolute.
- Error budget impact: spike does not consume > 10% of monthly error budget for the tenant.
- Telemetry completeness: >98% of requests in the simulation have full trace+span correlation and tenant tag.
- Customer communications: pre-notification delivered within SLA and post-simulation summary sent < 4 hours after completion.

Pre-simulation checklist (48–72 hours prior)
- Notify customer POC + legal (template below) and confirm acceptable windows.
- Schedule and reserve Eng-SRE and Runtime SME on calendar.
- Create simulation ticket in the incident system and link runbook.
- Warm synthetic workloads in tenant sandbox for baseline collection.
- Ensure KMS/HSM rotation windows do not overlap.

Simulation Runbook (controlled switchover example)
1. Preparation (T-30 minutes)
   1.1 Announce start to internal Slack channel #cs-ops and #oncall with timestamp.
   1.2 Verify telemetry baseline: collect last 30m p50/p95/throughput.
   1.3 Snapshot configuration: export routing table, model-variant pins, and KV cache stats.
2. Execute (T0)
   2.1 Trigger ingress route change using the routing-control API: 
```
POST https://control.redwood.internal/v1/route/switch
{
  "tenant_id": "TEN-01234",
  "from": "primary-ingress",
  "to": "fallback-ingress",
  "timeout_seconds": 30
}
```
   2.2 Observe the ingress metrics and confirm request flow changes in the dashboard (expected delta within 30s).
   2.3 If KV cache misses spike > 15% sustained for 2 minutes, engage Runtime SME to enable cache-warm policy: enable-cache-warm(TEN-01234).
3. Mitigation (if degraded)
   3.1 If p95 > 800ms for > 3 minutes, abort switchback: invoke route rollback API and notify customer.
   3.2 If error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes, escalate to Major Incident path and assign Incident Commander.
4. Stabilize (T+10–T+30 minutes)
   4.1 Confirm telemetry shows stable p95/p50 below thresholds.
   4.2 Collect evidence artifacts: links to trace samples, screenshots of dashboards, routing logs (store in simulation ticket).
   4.3 Send post-simulation internal update and customer summary (templates below).

Communications Templates
- Pre-notification (customer-facing, send 48–72h before):
"Dear <Customer POC>,
We plan to run a controlled failover simulation for your tenant <TEN-01234> on <DATE> between <START>–<END> (UTC). The exercise is to validate our redundant ingress and model-routing fallback. Expected impact: transient latency increase for up to 30s and a small increase in cache misses. No data modification is expected. Please reply to confirm the window is acceptable or propose an alternative.
Regards,
Customer Success — Redwood Inference"

- Immediate internal alert (Slack):
"[SIMULATION START] TEN-01234 — Controlled switchover starting now. Oncall: @marco. Runtime SME: @jordan. CS POC: <name>. Ticket: #INC-XXXX. Follow the runbook: <link>."

- Post-simulation customer summary (send within 4 hours):
"Summary: Controlled failover completed for TEN-01234 at <TIMESTAMP>. Outcome: PASS (or FAIL). Key metrics: p50: <value>, p95: <value>, error-rate: <value>. Actions taken: <list>. Evidence bundle: <link>. Next steps: <list>. Contact: <CS rep>."

Observability assertions and example queries
- Required metrics to capture during simulation: ingest_rate, request_latency_p50/p95, error_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, model_queue_length, gpu_utilization.
- Example PromQL (platform observability):
```
# p95 latency for tenant
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id="TEN-01234"}[1m])) by (le))

# KV cache hit ratio
sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total{tenant_id="TEN-01234"}[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_request_total{tenant_id="TEN-01234"}[1m]))
```

Evidence capture checklist (must be attached to simulation ticket)
- Dashboard screenshots (Ingress, Runtime, Telemetry)
- 10 representative traces with full span correlation
- Routing-control API audit log extract
- Export of the routing decision table before/after
- Customer notification emails (send + acknowledgement)

Escalation thresholds and routing
- Severity 3 (S3): transient anomalies that do not exceed thresholds — handled by Oncall Lead.
- Severity 2 (S2): p95 breach > 800ms or error-rate > 1% sustained 5m — engage Eng-Serving-Runtime and CS Director.
- Severity 1 (S1): sustained tenant unavailability or data integrity concern — invoke enterprise incident playbook and legal.

Regulatory/compliance attachments
- For regulated tenants, attach the signed Test Authorization Form (TAF) to the ticket before execution.
- Evidence retention: store artifacts in Compliance bucket with label tenant-failover-sim/YYYYMMDD and notify Legal.

Post-simulation retro and scoring
- Within 48 hours run a brief retro including CS, Eng-SRE, Runtime SME, and Telemetry.
- Scorecard (0–5 scale) per category: Execution, Observability, Communications, Customer Impact, Evidence Completeness.
- Required follow-ups (examples): increase cache-warm window, add additional span propagation, update routing-control safe-timeout to 45s.

Appendix: Quick CLI snippets
- Route switch (curl)
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"TEN-01234","from":"primary-ingress","to":"fallback-ingress","timeout_seconds":30}' \
  https://control.redwood.internal/v1/route/switch
```
- Extract audit log for ticket
```
redwood-cli logs query --ticket INC-XXXX --output ./evidence.zip
```

Related documents

Notes and caveats
- Always run in partnership with the customer for regulatory cutovers. When customer requests are more restrictive than this protocol, follow the customer-specified constraints and escalate to Legal.
- Simulation should be scheduled outside of the tenant's business-critical windows; if unavoidable, require explicit executive signoff.

End of document.
